options.D: The specific sign observed and the method used to detect it

explanation: Accurate records must specify what was found, such as fetal heart tones heard via Doppler, to establish valid clinical proof. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T3#BMP212_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the scheduled post-operative clinic visit?

options.A: To reverse the surgical tubal blockage
options.B: To prescribe strong hormonal replacement therapy
options.C: To inspect the wound and remove skin stitches
options.D: To perform a routine pregnancy test

explanation: The follow-up check ensures the incision is healing well and allows the midwife to remove non-absorbable sutures. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T12#BMP224_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal triage when women arrive at the clinic?

options.A: To distribute routine blood-building supplements to all pregnant women
options.B: To calculate the exact expected date of delivery for new clients
options.C: To rapidly sort women based on the urgency of their condition
options.D: To register women for their routine health insurance scheme

explanation: Triage is designed to prioritize care so that the most critically ill patients receive immediate attention. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which mineral is commonly lost from the body during standard diuretic therapy?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Iron

explanation: Diuretics frequently cause potassium to be washed out in the urine, which can lead to low potassium levels if not watched. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T6#BMP213_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary underlying problem in all forms of shock?

options.A: Complete failure of the central nervous system
options.B: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular oxygenation
options.C: Severe elevation in systemic arterial blood pressure
options.D: Sudden and permanent cessation of heart sounds

explanation: Shock fundamentally represents a failure of the circulatory system to supply tissues with enough oxygen and nutrients for normal function. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T4#BMP110_U7_T4_h1)

question: A pregnant woman presents with malaria. Which branch of microbiology studies the organism that causes this?

options.A: Virology
options.B: Bacteriology
options.C: Parasitology
options.D: Mycology

explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium species, which are microscopic parasites studied under parasitology. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T1#BMP116_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which part of the bacteria do macrolides attach to in order to stop protein production?

options.A: The bacterial circular DNA strand
options.B: The 50S ribosomal subunit
options.C: The outer cell wall peptidoglycan
options.D: The small 30S ribosomal subunit

explanation: Macrolides bind to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, which stops the bacteria from building new proteins. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T4#BMP124_U4_T4_h2)

question: Around what age does the rooting reflex normally disappear in a healthy infant?

options.A: 6 to 8 years
options.B: 9 to 12 months
options.C: 3 to 4 months
options.D: 1 to 2 weeks

explanation: As the higher brain centers mature over the first few months of life, the rooting reflex naturally fades away. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why can a sinus infection sometimes spread to the eye socket or the brain?

options.A: Blood flows backward away from the head during rest
options.B: Sinus bones dissolve completely during an infection
options.C: Bacteria can fly through the air inside the skull
options.D: The sinuses sit very close to the eyes and brain

explanation: The paranasal sinuses are located right next to the eye sockets and the skull cavity, allowing severe infections to spread to nearby areas. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the main job of dense bodies inside smooth muscle cells?

options.A: They transmit electrical impulses between organs
options.B: They store calcium ions needed for contraction
options.C: They produce ATP molecules for cellular energy
options.D: They serve as anchor points for thin actin filaments

explanation: Dense bodies act like anchor points, giving the pulling actin filaments something solid to latch onto during contraction. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T2#BMP111_U3_T2_h2)

question: Where is the pubic symphysis located in the pelvis?

options.A: At the very bottom tip of the tailbone
options.B: On the upper wing of the iliac crest
options.C: At the front, joining the two pubic bones
options.D: At the back, connecting the spine to the hip

explanation: The pubic symphysis sits right at the front middle, uniting the left and right pubic bones. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h3)

question: What happens to the severed ends of the fallopian tubes after a successful Pomeroy ligation?

options.A: They fuse back together automatically within a few weeks.
options.B: They absorb completely into the surrounding pelvic fat.
options.C: They attach directly to the wall of the urinary bladder.
options.D: They scar over and remain permanently separated and closed.

explanation: The absorbable suture allows the ends to separate and scar over as the suture dissolves, blocking egg passage. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T12#BMP224_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of constructing a concrete apron sloping away from a borehole wellhead?

options.A: To ensure the handpump mechanism remains securely anchored in the soil
options.B: To collect rainwater separately from the underground water supply
options.C: To prevent dirty wastewater from flowing back down into the water source
options.D: To provide a comfortable sitting area for women waiting to fetch water

explanation: A sloped concrete apron directs spilled water away from the borehole casing, stopping surface contaminants from seeping inward. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h3)

question: During a physical check, which finding points strongly toward a missed abortion?

options.A: A loud fetal heart sound is heard through a stethoscope
options.B: The cervix is fully dilated with active tissue extrusion
options.C: Uterine size is smaller than expected for gestational dates
options.D: Blood pressure is dangerously elevated above normal limits

explanation: Because growth has stopped and some tissue is slowly absorbed or fluids decrease, the uterus often feels smaller than it should be for the patient's expected weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h3)

question: How often should a mother's vital signs be checked during the first hour after a Caesarean section?

options.A: Every 2 hours
options.B: Once at the end of the hour
options.C: Every 15 minutes
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes in the first hour helps the midwife catch early signs of bleeding or anesthesia issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h5)

question: Where must the chest drainage collection system be placed relative to the patient?

options.A: Directly hanging on the top of the bed headboard
options.B: Below the level of the patient's chest
options.C: Higher than the insertion site to encourage flow
options.D: At the exact same height as the mattress

explanation: Gravity helps fluid drain away from the patient. Placing the unit below chest level stops fluid from flowing backward into the chest. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T11#BMP125_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the difference between quickening and examiner-palpated movement?

options.A: Quickening requires an ultrasound machine to verify, whereas palpation does not
options.B: Quickening occurs only in the third trimester, while palpation happens early in the first
options.C: Quickening is felt only by the mother, whereas palpated movement is felt by the clinician
options.D: Quickening is caused by gas, whereas palpated movement is caused by uterine contractions

explanation: Mother-reported quickening is a presumptive sign, while an examiner feeling the kicks makes it a positive sign. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T3#BMP212_U1_T3_h4)

question: What sound is typically heard through a stethoscope when listening to the chest of someone having an asthma attack?

options.A: Expiratory wheezing
options.B: Absent breath sounds universally
options.C: Fine crackles at lung bases
options.D: Loud pleural friction rubs

explanation: As air struggles to pass through narrowed bronchial tubes during breathing out, it creates a high-pitched whistling sound known as a wheeze. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T8#BMP125_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which finding is most reassuring regarding a two-week-old baby's nutrition status?

options.A: The birth weight has been successfully regained
options.B: The infant refuses to feed during the night
options.C: The baby sleeps continuously for ten hours
options.D: The stools are consistently hard and dry

explanation: Regaining birth weight by around two weeks of age confirms that milk transfer and intake are adequate. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h7)

question: What might an uneven (asymmetrical) rooting reflex suggest in a newborn delivered with vacuum assistance?

options.A: Local facial nerve injury
options.B: Congenital heart failure
options.C: Severe maternal infection
options.D: Generalized brain tumors

explanation: An uneven reflex on one side of the face often points to mild, temporary nerve trauma from an instrumental delivery. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h5)

question: How does the physical process of a missed abortion happen in the body?

options.A: Infection builds up immediately and creates a solid pelvic mass
options.B: Strong muscular spasms open the cervix wide within minutes
options.C: The placenta instantly grows larger to push out the dead tissue
options.D: Hormone levels drop and tissue detaches, but the cervix stays closed

explanation: When a pregnancy stops growing, hormone levels fall and the sac detaches from the uterine wall. However, if the cervix fails to open, the tissue stays trapped inside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h2)

question: A midwife finishes dressing an infected perineal wound. Where should she discard the soiled gauze?

options.A: In the puncture-resistant yellow sharps box
options.B: In the black general household waste bin
options.C: In the yellow biohazard waste bin
options.D: In an open basin on her desk

explanation: Gauze soiled with body fluids and pus is infectious waste and must go into the biohazard container. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h7)

question: Which of these actions goes against patient dignity during clinical teaching?

options.A: Discussing the patient's condition across her bed as if she were not present
options.B: Drawing privacy curtains around the bed before the examination
options.C: Exposing only the specific area needed for a physical check
options.D: Asking for permission before letting a student palpate the abdomen

explanation: Talking about a patient as if she is absent strips away her dignity and ignores her presence. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the normal job of inhibin in the female reproductive hormone cycle?

options.A: It directly stimulates milk production in ducts.
options.B: It suppresses pituitary FSH secretion.
options.C: It thickens the cervical mucus during ovulation.
options.D: It triggers the immediate release of an ovum.

explanation: Ovarian follicles release inhibin to help regulate and lower FSH production. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T1#BMP320_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do Hepatitis B and C lead to liver cancer over time?

options.A: By causing chronic inflammation and continuous tissue regeneration
options.B: By freezing all metabolic processes in liver cells
options.C: By stopping the production of bile
options.D: By replacing liver tissue with bone marrow

explanation: Long-term liver inflammation forces constant cell repair and division, increasing the chance of permanent genetic errors and cancer. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T4#BMP116_U4_T4_h3)

question: A ten-day-old baby in the nursery develops an infection while in the hospital. How is this classified?

options.A: Perinatal asphyxia
options.B: Early-onset sepsis
options.C: Congenital toxoplasmosis
options.D: Late-onset sepsis

explanation: Infections that show up after 72 hours of life, especially in hospital settings, are grouped as late-onset sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a main biological hazard faced by midwives in healthcare settings?

options.A: Agricultural dust from crop harvesting
options.B: Excessive noise from heavy factory machines
options.C: Toxic chemical fumes from industrial mining
options.D: Infectious pathogens and needle-stick injuries

explanation: Healthcare workers deal directly with patients and biological fluids, exposing them to infections and sharp injuries. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T1#BMP126_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is a major characteristic of a hard-to-reach community in healthcare terms?

options.A: Lacking easy access to standard health facilities
options.B: Being located inside major urban capital cities
options.C: Having too many private clinics operating at once
options.D: Refusing all forms of modern medicine completely

explanation: Hard-to-reach communities face physical, geographic, or financial barriers that prevent them from easily reaching established health centres. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which tissue makes up the largest part of a normal, healthy cervix?

options.A: Endocrine glandular tissue
options.B: Collagen and connective tissue matrix
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Smooth muscle cells

explanation: The cervix is mainly made of fibrous tissue and collagen, giving it the strength needed to hold a pregnancy securely. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why must a primary healthcare midwife build strong relationships with traditional community leaders?

options.A: To replace traditional herbal remedies with surgical operations
options.B: To collect taxes for building new tertiary hospitals
options.C: To build trust and encourage families to seek skilled care early
options.D: To take over the traditional leadership roles in the village

explanation: Engaging community leaders helps overcome cultural barriers and encourages pregnant women to visit the clinic for safe delivery. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T2#BMP117_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which micronutrient is routinely recommended alongside ORS because it helps repair the gut lining and shortens illness duration?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Zinc
options.C: Iron
options.D: Calcium

explanation: World Health Organization guidelines recommend daily zinc supplementation for children with diarrhea because it aids intestinal cell regeneration and immune response. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T1#BMP222_U3_T1_h6)

question: A client using CycleBeads reports that two of her cycles in the past six months lasted 24 days. What instruction should the midwife give?

options.A: Continue using CycleBeads but skip counting the short months.
options.B: Wait until her cycle stretches to 35 days before seeking help.
options.C: Switch to a different family planning method because her cycles are now irregular.
options.D: Move the rubber ring twice as fast during her next menstrual cycle.

explanation: Cycles outside the 26 to 32 day range do not meet safety criteria, meaning the client needs to switch to another contraceptive option. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T1#BMP224_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is it necessary to wait a few minutes after injecting local anesthesia before starting the repair?

options.A: To give the placenta time to separate from the uterine wall
options.B: To allow the vaginal tissues time to swell up for easier grasping
options.C: To give the drug time to numb the nerve endings effectively
options.D: To let the local bleeding stop completely on its own

explanation: Local anesthetics require a brief latency period to block nerve transmission so the patient does not feel pain during suturing. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h4)

question: What does a very large standard deviation tell a midwife about newborn birth weights in a ward?

options.A: The birth weights are widely spread out and vary greatly from the average
options.B: The weighing scale used by the nursing staff is broken and needs calibration
options.C: The average birth weight calculated for the babies is mathematically incorrect
options.D: Nearly all the babies born in the facility share almost the exact same weight

explanation: Standard deviation measures dispersion. A larger number indicates a greater spread of individual data points away from the mean. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T1#BMP225_U4_T1_h4)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks gets Hepatitis A. What is the usual outcome for her liver after recovery?

options.A: Delayed progression to primary liver cancer
options.B: Complete recovery without chronic carrier state
options.C: Lifelong shedding of the virus in her stool
options.D: Development of permanent liver cirrhosis

explanation: Hepatitis A is an acute infection that usually heals completely on its own, leaving the patient with lifelong immunity and no long-term liver trouble. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h2)

question: What key substance is missing in the lungs of a newborn with Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)?

options.A: Meconium protein
options.B: Gastric mucin
options.C: Amniotic fluid
options.D: Pulmonary surfactant

explanation: RDS happens when there is not enough surfactant. Surfactant lowers surface tension inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) to help keep them open. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T5#BMP220_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why must the midwife avoid twisting or rotating the vacuum cup while pulling?

options.A: It reverses the baby's heartbeat during labor
options.B: It will immediately rupture the mother's uterus
options.C: It can cause severe scalp damage and cup detachment
options.D: It pushes the baby back up into the abdominal cavity

explanation: Vacuum cups are designed only for straight traction; twisting motions tear the scalp skin and break the vacuum seal. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is checking length and head circumference alongside weight important for an SGA newborn?

options.A: It prevents the baby from developing neonatal jaundice.
options.B: It helps distinguish between symmetrical and asymmetrical growth restriction.
options.C: It calculates the exact amount of breastmilk the baby needs daily.
options.D: It proves the exact day the mother conceived her child.

explanation: Comparing head and length measurements to weight reveals whether growth restriction affected the whole body or spared the head. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T2#BMP220_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of antenatal care provided by skilled health personnel?

options.A: To safeguard maternal and fetal well-being
options.B: To secure hospital admission for delivery
options.C: To eliminate all labor pain completely
options.D: To determine the exact sex of the baby

explanation: Antenatal care is fundamentally designed to monitor and protect the health of both the mother and the developing fetus throughout the pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months of life help protect an infant against pneumonia?

options.A: It completely blocks all environmental air pollutants from entering the baby's lungs
options.B: It replaces the need for any routine childhood immunizations later in life
options.C: It provides maternal antibodies and immune factors that fight off infections
options.D: It prevents the infant from ever developing a fever or cough

explanation: Breastmilk contains protective immune factors and antibodies that strengthen the baby's mucosal defenses against respiratory pathogens. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T6#BMP125_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is obtaining proper informed consent essential during maternity care?

options.A: It replaces the need for documenting vital signs on a chart
options.B: It legally protects the hospital from paying financial fines
options.C: It honors the woman's right to understand and choose her care
options.D: It shortened the overall duration of the first stage of labor

explanation: Informed consent is about respecting autonomy, ensuring the woman understands procedures, risks, and alternatives before agreeing. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h4)

question: A nursing mother asks why her underarm sweat has a stronger smell than sweat on her arms. Which gland is responsible?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat cells
options.B: Eccrine sweat glands
options.C: Apocrine sweat glands
options.D: Sebaceous oil glands

explanation: Apocrine glands produce thicker secretions in areas like the armpits, which develop odors when skin bacteria break them down. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T7#BMP111_U4_T7_h2)

question: What must be completely destroyed during a valid sterilization process?

options.A: Visible dirt and dried blood stains on metal surfaces
options.B: All microorganisms including bacterial endospores
options.C: Fungi and viruses while ignoring bacterial spores
options.D: Only active bacteria floating on the instrument surface

explanation: Sterilization is an absolute state meaning zero living organisms or spores remain on the processed item. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h2)

question: Why is diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in an expectant mother so dangerous for the baby?

options.A: The placenta stores excess ketones and releases them to the fetus
options.B: High glucose levels cause the fetus to stop growing completely
options.C: Maternal ketones destroy the umbilical cord blood vessels instantly
options.D: Maternal acidosis quickly reduces blood flow through the placenta

explanation: Severe acid-base imbalance in the mother compromises uteroplacental perfusion, cutting off oxygen and nutrients to the baby. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T3#BMP216_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does bedside teaching help students build good communication skills?

options.A: By forcing them to memorize medical terminology in silence
options.B: By letting them practice speaking empathetically with women in pain or anxiety
options.C: By limiting their conversations strictly to written documentation
options.D: By teaching them how to lecture large groups of people

explanation: Interacting directly with real patients teaches students how to offer emotional comfort and clear explanations. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why are near misses considered valuable subjects for clinical safety investigations?

options.A: They require no paperwork or administrative committee review
options.B: They prove that current maternity guidelines are completely flawless
options.C: They reveal hidden system flaws before actual harm occurs
options.D: They guarantee that no patient will ever complain later

explanation: Studying near misses allows hospitals to fix broken processes proactively before an identical scenario results in severe injury or death. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h5)

question: What happens if a stimulus is too weak to reach the threshold of -55 mV?

options.A: A very slow action potential travels down the axon
options.B: No action potential will be generated at all
options.C: The cell permanently loses its resting potential
options.D: Only potassium channels open to create a small spike

explanation: Nerve signals follow an all-or-none rule. If the stimulus does not reach the -55 mV threshold, the neuron simply does not fire. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h3)

question: If a pregnant woman's lab results show a creatinine level right in the middle of the normal non-pregnant range, what might this actually mean?

options.A: Eating too much protein
options.B: A completely normal state
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: Potential underlying kidney issues

explanation: Normal pregnancy lowers serum creatinine through increased filtration, so a standard non-pregnant value can actually point to reduced kidney function in an expectant mother. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is bedside teaching different from a normal classroom lecture?

options.A: It prevents students from making any clinical mistakes
options.B: It removes the need for patient consent during tutorials
options.C: It allows students to pass exams without studying theory
options.D: It exposes learners to the authentic environment of maternity units

explanation: Real clinical settings provide practical experience with actual patients that a classroom cannot fully replicate. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT lost automatically when a patient is admitted involuntarily?

options.A: The obligation to stay within the secure hospital perimeter
options.B: The immediate control over their physical daily movements
options.C: The legal restriction on leaving the psychiatric ward freely
options.D: The right to humane treatment and protection from abuse

explanation: Involuntary status restricts liberty, but patients never lose their fundamental right to be treated with dignity and protected from abuse. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T4#BMP223_U1_T4_h4)

question: What exam finding strongly points to an incomplete abortion?

options.A: A thick mucous plug blocking the entire vaginal entrance
options.B: An open cervical os with active bleeding or visible tissue
options.C: A completely closed cervix with no sign of any discharge
options.D: Severe greenish-yellow foul-smelling discharge alone

explanation: When the cervix is open and blood or tissue is passing, it shows the uterus is trying to empty an incomplete pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h3)

question: How does erythromycin work to stop bacterial growth in newborn eye infections?

options.A: By blocking cellular DNA replication enzymes
options.B: By inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis
options.C: By altering the pH level of the tear film
options.D: By dissolving the outer cell wall completely

explanation: Erythromycin attaches to bacterial ribosomes to stop them from making essential proteins. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T2#BMP213_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of postnatal care provided by a midwife right inside the family's home?

options.A: Providing routine cooking lessons for the new family
options.B: Delivering professional midwifery services inside the family home
options.C: Replacing all hospital checkups with television consultations
options.D: Conducting mandatory immunization drives at local schools

explanation: Domiciliary care means taking clinical assessment and support directly to where the mother and baby live after birth. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason a patient might experience a self-care deficit?

options.A: Lacking knowledge about a new diagnosis
options.B: Suffering from a debilitating illness
options.C: Possessing high personal health literacy
options.D: Experiencing severe physical exhaustion

explanation: High health literacy supports and enhances self-care agency rather than causing a deficit. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is a wide subpubic angle important during the second stage of labour?

options.A: It reduces the risk of postpartum haemorrhage
options.B: It allows the placenta to deliver faster
options.C: It prevents premature rupture of the membranes
options.D: It gives the foetal head enough space to pass under the pubic arch

explanation: A wide subpubic angle permits safe extension and crowning of the baby's head beneath the pubic bone. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h4)

question: What usually happens when the normal acid level in the vagina drops?

options.A: Fungal spores grow faster inside the uterus.
options.B: Normal bacteria are completely destroyed by a drop in body temperature.
options.C: Harmful bacteria multiply quickly when protective lactic acid goes down.
options.D: Lactobacilli need an alkaline environment to make hydrogen peroxide.

explanation: Lactobacilli keep the vaginal environment acidic and safe; when they decrease, harmful bacteria can take over. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h1)

question: A woman carrying triplets is admitted to the labor ward at 36 weeks. What is the standard and safest route of delivery for her babies?

options.A: Immediate induction of labor with oxytocin
options.B: Immediate vacuum extraction for all three fetuses
options.C: Emergency trial of unassisted vaginal delivery
options.D: Planned elective caesarean section

explanation: Higher-order multiples like triplets carry high risks during vaginal delivery, making a planned caesarean section the safest standard of care. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T8#BMP311_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to treat viral infections?

options.A: Antibiotics target bacterial structures like cell walls that viruses do not possess
options.B: Antibiotics are quickly destroyed by the immune system of pregnant women
options.C: Bacterial cells are much smaller than any known viral particle
options.D: Viruses hide inside red blood cells where drugs cannot reach them

explanation: Antibiotics disrupt bacterial processes, but viruses use completely different structures and host machinery, making antibacterial drugs ineffective. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T1#BMP116_U4_T1_h1)

question: What dental issue can happen if a fetus is exposed to tetracyclines during tooth development?

options.A: Complete absence of adult teeth
options.B: Rapid jawbone fracture
options.C: Severe gum infection
options.D: Permanent yellow-brown tooth discoloration

explanation: When the drug binds with calcium in developing tooth enamel, it causes a permanent yellow-brown color change. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T5#BMP124_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which temporary organ serves as the physiological bridge between mother and fetus?

options.A: The placenta
options.B: The yolk sac
options.C: The decidua
options.D: The amnion

explanation: The placenta is the temporary organ responsible for connecting maternal circulation with fetal needs during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T2#BMP210_U5_T2_h1)

question: How did the Aro Village Mental Health Programme change patient care?

options.A: By housing patients with local families in nearby villages for care
options.B: By stopping all forms of medication and relying solely on surgery
options.C: By banning family members from visiting psychiatric facilities
options.D: By transferring all patients to permanent high-security prison cells

explanation: The village system placed patients into local households, reducing isolation and preserving their community ties. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T2#BMP223_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard family planning medical history?

options.A: Menstrual cycle length and regularity
options.B: Recent building construction permits
